title: The Friend Of My Friend
gist: Xi Jinping's expected mid-September 2026 trip to India — his first in seven years, with a 400-person delegation — signals a thaw in the one broken link in the Eurasian great-power triangle. The piece's core logic is that Russia, cut off from its 150-year commodity business with Western Europe, needs its two remaining large non-Western buyers, China and India, to stop feuding.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping is expected to travel to India in mid-September 2026 with a 400-person delegation, his first visit there in seven years.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Delegation size and a seven-year gap point to a substantive commercial agenda, not a photo-op — watch for trade, border and investment-access announcements that would reprice India-China supply-chain and tariff risk.
insights.quote: In mid-September, Chinese president Xi Jinping is expected to visit India for the first time in seven years with a 400-person-strong delegation.
insights.locator: In mid-September, Chinese president Xi Jinping

insights.claim: The China-India relationship, described as frosty in recent years, is thawing, and the scale of the planned Xi visit is the marker of that shift.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A genuine detente between Asia's two largest economies would loosen a persistent risk premium on regional trade and on Indian manufacturers exposed to Chinese components and capital.
insights.quote: This visit seems important as it seems to mark a thaw in the Indian-Chinese relationship; a relationship that has definitely been somewhat frosty in recent years.
insights.locator: This visit seems important as it seems

insights.claim: Among the great powers of Eurasia, the India-China link is the anomaly: China is now very close to Russia and India has kept a friendly relationship with Moscow since independence in 1947, yet the transitive rule that the friend of my friend is my friend has never held between Delhi and Beijing.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Use the triangle as the map for Eurasian alignment: the India-China edge is the only unresolved one, so it is where the largest geopolitical repricing can happen and where headlines will cluster.
insights.quote: when it comes to the India-China relationship, it simply has not been true that “the friend of my friend is my friend.”

insights.claim: India's pro-Moscow orientation is structural rather than opportunistic, dating continuously to its 1947 independence, which limits how far Western pressure can pull Delhi away from Russia.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Discount scenarios in which India decisively breaks with Russia over sanctions; Indian buyers of discounted Russian commodities are more durable than sanctions headlines imply.
insights.quote: India, since independence in 1947, has always maintained a very friendly relationship with Moscow
insights.locator: China is now very close friends with Russia

insights.claim: Russia's 150-year business model — extracting commodities and selling them into Western Europe — is now clearly compromised, forcing a permanent search for replacement demand.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat the Europe-Russia commodity link as structurally severed rather than cyclically interrupted: European industrial input costs stay reset higher, and Russian export volumes must keep rerouting east.
insights.quote: for 150 years, Russia’s business model was to extract commodities and sell these to Western Europe. This business model is now clearly compromised.
insights.locator: But secondly, and much more importantly

insights.claim: Outside the Western world, only two countries constitute meaningful marginal commodity demand — China and India — so Russia's export redirection is concentrated in just two counterparties.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Buyer concentration hands Beijing and Delhi pricing power over Russian barrels and bulk commodities; watch Russian export discounts as the observable measure of that leverage.
insights.quote: when it comes to commodity demand ex-Western-World, two countries stand out: China and India
insights.locator: And when it comes to commodity demand

insights.claim: Russia has a direct commercial stake in a China-India rapprochement because it now depends on both as commodity buyers and, with few remaining allies, cannot afford friction between the two.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Read Moscow as an active promoter of the thaw rather than a bystander — an implied third party working to keep the India-China detente alive, which raises the odds it persists.
insights.quote: The fact that Russia’s two most important friends do not get along is a bummer for Russia.
